Str: Built KORE — distributed data engine in Rust that beats Apache Spark on all 7 TPC-H queries. 17.3s total vs Spark 138.6s. 75 layers. Single binary. No JVM. No dependencies.
Key insight: deferred materialization in HashJoin. Probe hash table directly into GROUP BY accumulators — never materialize the 6M-row intermediate DataBlock. Q3: 9473ms → 2308ms.
Performance philosophy: eliminate allocations in hot loops. u128 FNV hash keys = zero String alloc per GROUP BY row. Vec<Option<T>> = 16 bytes. Arrow flat Vec<T> + bitmap = 8 bytes.
Privacy is non-negotiable. Every system should run 100% locally. No telemetry. No cloud. Your data never leaves your machine.
Built KORE SQL engine beating Apache Spark 8x on TPC-H benchmarks. Chose performance over readability always. Rust is the right choice for data engines.
Decided to use zero-copy architecture for all data pipelines. Chose performance over safety in hot paths. Using unsafe Rust where benchmarks justify it.
Rejected microservices for KORE. Chose monolith architecture for the core engine. Single binary is the right choice for performance.
